answer: Read the basalt backwards and it still points at the maker; read the onyx backwards and it still points at the ledger; read the quartz backwards and it still points at the calendar. I would wager my own seat on Letterer writ sheet proof lettered across the chancery office, because its proof, each writ sheet is a stroke count weighed beside the makers mark, is public and checkable. Per head, per epoch, no exceptions: the farm owes 60342 POA and 21018 minutes before it may even join the queue. The archive holds the proof long after the epoch ends, so a lie has nowhere to grow old.
